title: Aq Qoyunlu
capsule: The Aq Qoyunlu ('White Sheep' Turkmen) were a confederal state that dominated eastern Anatolia, Azerbaijan, and Persia from the mid-fifteenth century. Under Uzun Hasan (r. 1453–1478), who defeated and killed the rival Kara Koyunlu ruler Jahan Shah in 1467 and then crushed the Timurid Abu Sa'id in 1469, the confederation reached its apogee, holding territory from the Euphrates to Khurasan and cultivating diplomatic ties with Venice against the Ottomans. Uzun Hasan's defeat by Mehmed II at the Battle of Otlukbeli (1473) checked westward expansion, and after his death succession quarrels opened the dynasty to Safavid pressure; Shah Ismail I annihilated the last Aq Qoyunlu force at the Battle of Almut in 1503 and extinguished the dynasty by 1508.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Core territories in Azerbaijan and eastern Anatolia are documented through Ottoman and Venetian diplomatic records and Persian chronicles. Peripheral zones, particularly in Kurdistan and the Zagros, are reconstructed from tribal tribute patterns and are approximate.
